standard: Cloudflare Turnstile, Managed mode, server-side Siteverify, single-use tokens, fail-closed (plan P-2) for HUMAN forms; machine surfaces are credential-gated instead (spec 004). Checked by tools/check-turnstile.mjs in CI.

entries.name: Ellie anonymous session creation (panel, embedded website chat)
Ellie session creation + listing via the internal (app BFF) mode of the same route
entries.reason: Server-to-server only: requires the ELLIE_INTERNAL_KEY secret plus a BFF-validated signed-in account context. The anonymous mode of this route is the protected one (ellie-anonymous-session).

entries.name: In-session Ellie actions: messages, uploads, finalize, escalate (support ticket), upload read/delete
entries.reason: Possession credential: every action requires the session token issued at (Turnstile-gated) creation, or the internal key for the signed-in path. Escalate files the support ticket from inside an already-gated session.

entries.name: Ellie analyses API (create, approve, edit)
entries.reason: Credential-gated machine surface: API key, OAuth token, or the internal key (gateAnalysis), with the engine re-checking account ownership and staff status for approvals.

entries.name: API action routes (newsletter-subscribe, support-ticket, ellie-session)
entries.reason: Machine endpoints behind the shared credential gate (API key or OAuth token with the named scope, C-10/C-13). Spec 004: Turnstile never applies to agent traffic — a non-browser client cannot complete a browser challenge. The human consent that can authorize these actions is itself Turnstile-protected (website repo registry, app-oauth-consent).

entries.name: API tool routes (cost estimator, scoping checklist, timeline calculator)
entries.reason: Machine compute endpoints for agent clients behind the same credential gate; no human form exists on this surface (spec 004).

entries.name: MCP server endpoint (all tools)
entries.reason: Machine protocol endpoint: API-key/OAuth credentials, quotas, and per-tool kill switches are the controls (spec 004). Browser challenges must never sit in front of agent traffic.
